title: Rescue
emergency: Animal injured or in danger right now? Call the official contacts below or find the nearest emergency vet.
accountBody: To report an animal that needs rescue and see alerts in your area, create an account. The guide and contacts work without one.

guide.title: Step-by-step rescue guide
guide.body: Assessment, vet, quarantine and aftercare, with a checklist.

report.title: Report an animal for rescue
report.body: Share the location so NGOs, agencies and volunteers can go there. Any animal counts.

contacts.title: Official contacts
contacts.intro: Call according to the case. These numbers work anywhere in Brazil.
contacts.ccz: For dogs and cats, also look for animal protection NGOs and your city's Zoonosis Control Center (CCZ).

advice.environmental: Wild or marine animal: the environmental agency does the rescue. Don't try to catch it or take it home (it can be dangerous and keeping wildlife without authorization is a crime).
advice.livestock: Horse, cattle or another large animal: on a road or at risk of an accident, call 190 or 193. City halls often have a pickup service.
advice.domestic: Dog or cat: if injured, take it to a vet. NGOs and your city's CCZ can help with sheltering.

open.title: Rescue alerts
open.body: Animals needing help, nearest first (when location is allowed).
open.emptyBody: Good news! When someone reports an animal that needs rescue, it shows up here.

kinds.livestock: Cattle, pig or other farm animal

form.title: Report an animal for rescue
form.intro: Tell where the animal is and how it is. The exact location is only shown to people with an account.
form.wildWarning: Wild animal: keep your distance, don't try to catch it and call the environmental agency. Your alert helps the team find the place.
form.descriptionHint: E.g. dog with an injured paw, scared, near the bus stop.
form.locationHelp: Required: where the animal is. Only people with an account see it.
form.referenceHint: E.g. behind the market, under the bridge.
form.contactHint: So rescuers can talk to you. Only people with an account see it.

delete.title: Delete this alert?
delete.body: The alert and its photos will be deleted.

gone.title: Alert not found
gone.body: It may have been deleted by whoever reported it.

guide.wildWarning: A wild animal (bird, snake, opossum, monkey...)? DO NOT try to catch it. Keep people away and call the environmental agency (in Brazil, IBAMA or the Environmental Police at 190).
guide.vetOnly: Medicines, vaccines and dewormers: only as a vet advises. The app never recommends medicines or doses.
guide.finishBody: Now the animal needs a home. You can list it for responsible adoption or add it as your pet to track its health.

approach.title: Assessment and approach
approach.summary: Check the animal's condition, earn its trust with food and restrain it safely.

safety.title: Keep yourself safe first
safety.body: Watch from a distance. An animal in pain or afraid may bite or scratch. On a road, signal and ask for help.

assess.title: Check the animal's condition
assess.body: Is it breathing? Bleeding? Can it walk? Is it trapped? Note what you see: it helps the vet.

calm.title: Approach calmly
calm.body: Crouch sideways, speak softly, no sudden moves and no staring. Let the animal come to you.

food.title: Offer food and water
food.body: A little food helps build trust. If there's a serious injury, don't insist: the vet may need it to be fasting.

contain.title: Restrain it safely
contain.body: Use a towel, blanket, leash or carrier. Wear thick gloves if possible. Never hold it by the neck.

transport.title: Transport carefully
transport.body: A carrier or a lined cardboard box with holes. Keep the animal warm, in a dark and quiet place.

vet.title: Veterinary care
vet.summary: Take the animal to a vet for emergency exams, wound care and health planning.

emergency.title: Emergency exams
emergency.body: The vet assesses the overall condition and decides which exams are needed.

wounds.title: Wound care
wounds.body: Don't use human medicines or home remedies. Only what the vet prescribes.

deworm.title: Deworming
deworm.body: Done as the vet advises, according to age and weight.

vaccines.title: Vaccines
vaccines.body: The vet decides which vaccines and when, after examining the animal.

neuter.title: Plan neutering
neuter.body: Agree on the best time with the vet. Look for free or low-cost neutering programs in your city.

records.title: Keep the records
records.body: Photos of prescriptions, exams and the vaccination card. You can keep everything in the app, in the pet's profile.

quarantine.title: Isolation and quarantine
quarantine.summary: Keep the animal apart from other animals for 7 to 14 days to watch for symptoms and incubating diseases.

separate.title: Keep it apart
separate.body: A room or space just for it, away from your other animals.

days.title: Count 7 to 14 days
days.body: That's the time for incubating diseases to show up. Follow the period your vet recommends.

observe.title: Watch for signs
observe.body: Coughing, sneezing, diarrhea, vomiting, eye discharge or no appetite: tell the vet.

hygiene.title: Keep things clean
hygiene.body: Wash your hands after handling the animal and clean its space every day.

ownItems.title: Its own items
ownItems.body: Separate bowls, bed and toys, not shared with other animals.

aftercare.title: Care after the rescue
aftercare.summary: Provide shelter (foster or permanent home), proper food, affection and start a responsible adoption.

shelter.title: Shelter
shelter.body: A foster or permanent home, protected from sun, rain and cold.

food.title: Proper food
food.body: Food suited to the species and age, and fresh water always. Ask the vet if in doubt.

affection.title: Affection and patience
affection.body: Respect the animal's pace: many arrive scared. Trust comes little by little.

adoption.title: Responsible adoption
adoption.body: Share photos and health information, interview candidates and sign an adoption agreement.

followUp.title: Follow up
followUp.body: Ask the adopter for news, especially in the first weeks.
